summary:
Allwork.Space republishes a Reuters report that OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Financial Services, a vertical version of ChatGPT aimed at investment bankers and equity researchers. The product combines OpenAI's newest model with licensed financial data sets built directly into the tool, and was developed with Morgan Stanley and Evercore acting as design partners.

The launch is framed as part of a broader trend of AI vendors building products for regulated industries where data governance and security dominate buying decisions. The offering extends ChatGPT Enterprise's existing security controls, including role-based access and encryption, and lets compliance teams export workspace logs into audit workflows.

The service runs on GPT-6 Astra, which OpenAI says improves retrieval across financial data tools, financial reasoning, and output accuracy. Described use cases include multi-source research, building financial models, and generating client materials such as pitchbooks using a firm's own templates.

Bundled data sources include Daloopa, LSEG News, PitchBook, Crunchbase and Quartr, covering earnings transcripts, financial statements and company fundamentals. OpenAI says this data is indexed on its own infrastructure to improve retrieval and citation quality. LSEG is noted as the sole distributor of Reuters news, financial data and real-time alerts to global financial professionals. Firms with existing data subscriptions can connect them via integrations with FactSet, S&P Global, Preqin and Datasite.

OpenAI says it intends to broaden the available financial data and further train models to identify, interpret and apply that information to tasks historically done by experienced analysts, and to expand the product beyond investment banking and equity research into the wider financial services sector. Reporting is credited to Akash Sriram and Krystal Hu, edited by Devika Syamnath.
